note: RFC 4271 Section 9.1.2 states: If either the immediate next-hop or the IGP cost to the NEXT_HOP (where the NEXT_HOP is resolved through an IGP route) changes, Phase 2 Route Selection MUST be performed again. Independently re-read all six tagged occurrences and their real resolver, production subscriber, candidate extraction/selection and Loc-RIB mirroring producers. The immediate-hop unit drains initial and resulting no-op selection lookups, changes only the interior gateway at fixed metric 10, and requires candidate extraction to observe that new gateway while keeping the received BGP NEXT_HOP and no AIGP before and after. Its positive record disables next-hop change detection. Its negative native break corrupts received-NEXT_HOP mirroring and also fails initial preservation, so that red is not attributed solely to post-change reselection. The newly tagged cost-only unit keeps every existing test statement unchanged: two real Loc-RIB interior covers start at costs A10/B20, two stored iBGP paths have equal earlier ranking attributes and no AIGP, and the initially preferred A opposes later peer-address fallback. Changing only A's interior cost to 30 then 5 requires the mirrored selected route to move A to B and back to A, without another BGP input or a direct selector call. Its current native record preserves the initial production scan and omits only subscriber-driven repeated selection; clean passes, while the named mutated test fails specifically after A's cost rises to 30 because B never becomes selected. The existing retained-input loss/restoration unit and both internal/forked Linux daemon carriers additionally exercise selection changes on interior-cover availability without another UPDATE, with real ingress and actual BGP-best/Loc-RIB/kernel observations for the latter. Their trigger cuts preserve initial selection and fail after cover changes; these live scenarios do not separately claim cost-only daemon/forked/kernel reselection. The immediate-hop and cost-only triggers are now both directly asserted and discriminated within the bounded in-process IPv4 production subscriber, with distinct preservation controls, so the previous cost-only tagging/recording gap is closed. This does not prove every route-ranking criterion, prospective-recursion integration or packet forwarding.
